findings.title: Immutability model is security theater given orchestrator DROP TRIGGER rights
findings.evidence: "the orchestrator also has DROP TRIGGER privilege (it's the only DB user in hackathon scope). A malicious or buggy orchestrator could drop triggers, mutate rows, and recreate triggers"
findings.problem: The entire append-only guarantee collapses under a single compromised or buggy orchestrator process; triggers provide no protection against the sole writer.
findings.why_it_matters: Undermines the claimed "defense-in-depth" and "foundation" for 21 CFR Part 11 / design audit logs; adversarial orchestrator can rewrite history while leaving valid-looking chain and triggers.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove DB-level triggers from the threat model or enforce via separate read-only DB role, event triggers that cannot be dropped by app user, or external immutable log service. Label current design as non-immutable.

findings.title: Session isolation depends on untrustworthy workstation_id as security boundary
findings.location: 6.1 Open or Resume session code block and SDR-04-005
findings.evidence: "WHERE addin_session_id = @AddinSessionId AND workstation_id = @WorkstationId" and "UPDATE dhf.sessions SET ended_at = NOW() WHERE ended_at IS NULL AND workstation_id = @WorkstationId"
findings.problem: Assumes workstation_id cannot be spoofed, cloned, or shared across VMs/containers; advisory lock and close-other-sessions logic both rely on it.
findings.why_it_matters: Enables cross-instance session hijacking, premature session termination, or chain forking when the opposite assumption (adversarial or duplicated workstation identity) is true.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove workstation_id-based close logic and scoping; rely solely on unique AddinSessionId with stronger machine fingerprint or accept global visibility of all sessions per user.

findings.title: Hash canonicalization lists create brittle synchronization point with schema and DTOs
findings.evidence: Static arrays in DhfHashColumns.HashedColumns and ToolCallHashColumns.HashedColumns; "feature_tree_before and feature_tree_after (the raw JSONB blobs) are NOT in the hash input"
findings.problem: Any added column, renamed field, or DTO change not perfectly mirrored in the two static lists silently breaks validation or creates unverifiable historical entries.
findings.why_it_matters: Complexity inflation: the design chose two-level manual column lists over canonicalizing the already-defined DhfTurnContext DTO once; future schema evolution (inevitable) triggers rework of every validator and test.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace column lists with single canonical JSON serialization of the entire DhfTurnContext (excluding implementation IDs) plus ordered child array; derive record_hash and tool_calls_hash from that single source of truth.

findings.title: Writer computes its own hashes; no external witness or WORM storage for regulatory intent
findings.location: Section 12 Regulatory Framing Gap Analysis and entire AppendTurnAsync implementation
findings.evidence: orchestrator computes tipHash, toolCallsHash, then RecordHash before INSERT; "Hash chain + DB triggers + defense-in-depth" listed as partial Part 11 coverage
findings.problem: If the orchestrator (the sole writer) is malicious or buggy it can fabricate any transcript, tool calls, and matching hashes; chain validates but contains chosen lies.
findings.why_it_matters: Contradicts the "immutability enforcement" and "design audit log foundation" framing; true regulatory audit logs require separation between event generator and logger or cryptographic commitment before write.
findings.proposed_fix: Either move hash computation and chain validation into a separate privileged service the orchestrator calls, or use a blockchain-style external witness service. Update Section 12 to stop claiming foundation status.

findings.title: Deep validation creates brittle external dependency on filesystem state and retention policy
findings.location: 10.2 Deep Validation and ACC-02 acceptance criterion
findings.evidence: "Recomputes screenshot_before_sha256 and screenshot_after_sha256 from file bytes on disk"; "Screenshots must be retained through ACC-02 execution. cleanup-screenshots.ps1 MUST NOT be run"
findings.problem: Validation success now depends on perfect alignment between DB, on-disk files, and test orchestration; any cleanup, move to cloud storage, or container restart breaks it.
findings.why_it_matters: Turns an audit property into a fragile integration test that contradicts normal operational needs (cleanup). Edge case of missing files is downgraded to warning, weakening the guarantee.
findings.proposed_fix: Store screenshot SHA-256 at capture time only; drop runtime file recomputation from deep validation or make screenshots optional attachments with their hashes embedded in the immutable entry.
